key_insight: Choosing how to group commuting Pauli measurements can be cast as a binary optimization problem, and optimizing these groups materially reduces the sampling cost of quantum energy estimation.
engineering_relevance: This work provides a practical route to lower measurement overhead in variational quantum algorithms, which can directly improve efficiency on near-term quantum hardware.
method: Formulate fully commuting measurement grouping as a MILP clique-selection problem for non-overlapping groups.
Use optimized groups as initialization for iterative coefficient splitting (MILP-ICS) to improve overlapping measurement strategies.
Introduce O-clique to optimize overlapping commuting supports via candidate-clique selection and coefficient profiles.
evidence_signal: Across benchmark molecular Hamiltonians, approximate-covariance optimized groupings reduced the non-overlapping measurement requirement by 51.8% on average versus sorted insertion, and MILP-based methods also outperformed SI-based strategies on lattice Hamiltonians.
watch_item: The best performance depends on covariance approximations and optimization overhead, so the method may be less attractive if classical preprocessing cost is too high for the target problem size.
paper_title: Binary Optimization of Measurement Groupings for Quantum Energy Estimation
